# Dev

Invocation: `kc-dev-flow-2:dev`

Package root: /Users/kent/conductor/workspaces/kc-claude-plugins/colombo/.context/dev2-adoption/worktree/.worktrees/spacedock-ensign-model-roster-per-repo/kc-dev-flow-2
`<package>` in this skill and its linked files is this root. If the value above
is not an absolute path, the root is two directories above this `SKILL.md`.

Read the [framework](../../README.md). This is a start/resume entry, not a worker
stage or a second workflow controller. Claude's packaged command is
`/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`; bare `/dev` is not a promised cross-host alias.

Resolve the absolute project root, explicit workflow directory and intended work
item from the request and authoritative project/task records. Reuse established
context; do not guess between projects or tasks. Read applicable project
conventions and the existing context needed for the requested work.

After resolving the code root, run `python3 <package>/scripts/learning.py --repo
<absolute-code-root> notices --all`. Present relevant unread learning results (items
with `unread` true) to the user, distinguishing pending/uncertain, no-change, local proposal, PR and observed
merge; pending proposals are not active rules. Only after actual presentation,
run `ack --job <job> --expected <notice_digest>` for each shown snapshot. Context
injection or reading alone is not presentation. A changed digest stays unread;
interruption may repeat a notice. Settle every delivery shown `open`, acknowledged or not, by reading its PR
with `gh pr view` as learn's `Follow the delivery to a recorded end` says, before presenting.
Read failure holds that learning action, not
unrelated approved development. This entry-level check is not a host SessionStart
hook. Use [learn](../learn/SKILL.md) for an explicitly requested named-task loop;
notices do not authorize evaluation, delivery, retry or merge.

For existing work, preserve its recorded variant/profile, approved outcome,
scope, non-goals and stop condition. Read current state, reports and delivery
status instead of assuming a prior conversation is current. An invalid profile,
conflicting records or missing authority holds the dependent action; return only
the unresolved decision to the user. Do not restart approved design or ask again
for an unchanged selection.

For new work without a profile selection, establish the intended outcome and
recommend a profile using the framework's intended use and applicable shared
profile principles. Ask the user to select it before profile-dependent work.
An explicit valid selection is sufficient; FO records it with the variant in
the work item through the existing workflow. Recommendation is not selection.
For new work that adds a capability no journey map holds, ask once, before recommending a profile, whether to draw a story map first with kc-journey-map (`map`, `plan-release`, then `review-release`, which interrogates the release before splitting it). Record the result on each task as the workflow's `Release review:` line, or `Release review: not needed: <his words>`.

Hand the resolved project root, explicit workflow directory, work item, approved
selection/scope and bounded outcome to `spacedock:first-officer`, with this
skill's `Package root:` value, which FO writes into the scope notes of every
worker dispatch and follow-up message with a line telling the worker to send its completion
message to `main`, because the completion block Spacedock appends names `team-lead`. Retain that
workflow directory as `--workflow-dir` on SD commands; cwd alone is not the
binding. If FO is already active, continue there. SD owns stage selection, live
worker availability, dispatch, reports, gates and recovery; a resumed FO does
not establish that its old worker still exists. An entity sitting in a stage
declared `gate: true` is excluded from `spacedock status --next` and from
`--boot`'s DISPATCHABLE table before the concurrency check runs (Spacedock
v0.27.0, `internal/status/format.go`, `dispatchAnalysis`, reason `gate`), so an
empty dispatchable view does not mean no worker is available; three of this
workflow's five stages (`backlog`, `ideation`, `validation`) declare `gate: true`,
so that empty view is this workflow's normal case, not the exception. Stage
skills own profile routing and load the selected references in each worker's
context.

Before each worker dispatch and on resume, run `python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py
<workflow-dir>/README.md`. Exit 1 means the README FO follows differs from the trunk's,
exit 2 that it could not be compared; hold the dispatch, show the Captain the printed
remedy or cause, and wait. Do not run the remedy or move the checkout yourself. This
sentence sits here because a README old enough to be wrong may not contain it.

If adoption is absent or the selected profile does not match the ordered stage
graph, follow the [SD adoption reference](../../references/sd/adoption.md) through
`spacedock:commission` or `spacedock:refit` before dispatch. Invoking this entry does
not migrate an old variant, rewrite a workflow or install a package. Keep existing
work on its recorded variant unless a migration is explicitly approved. This
entry grants no new repair, approval, delivery or route-exception authority.

# Repository stage workers

## Adoption and introducing sync

Preserve an existing `.dev2/model-roster.json`; startup and ordinary sync do not
ask again or rewrite it. Ask only when the workflow frontmatter lists `paseo`
and the Codex provider is available. Otherwise ask nothing, write nothing and
retain README behavior. For eligible adoption or introducing sync without an
existing roster, display the complete [recommendation](model-roster-defaults.json)
and ask through the host's question UI:

> Stage workers: ideation Astra/high, implementation Sol/high, validation Astra/high,
> all Codex through Paseo. Save this shared repository choice or customize it?

Offer Accept and Customize. Preselection is not an answer. Cancel, empty response
or silence writes nothing, including no directory. Accept prepares the displayed
file; Customize collects each stage's exact tuple one at a time. Supported models
are `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6.1-sol`, with explicit `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`,
`max` or `ultra` effort, provider `codex` and host `paseo`. Other choices return to FO.
Set `selected_from` to the selected package version and `decision` to the explicit
answer reference; these are caller-recorded provenance, not authenticated consent.
Show the complete three-row candidate in the existing configuration review before
committing `<code-root>/.dev2/model-roster.json` through the repository's normal
change path. Explicit later edits or deletion take that same reviewed path.
Choosing Paseo does not enable its extension or grant access.

## Stage launch or continuation

Before record checks and Spacedock build, run
`python3 <package>/scripts/model_roster.py resolve --code-root <absolute-code-worktree-root> --stage <stage>`.
For validation repeat `--author-record <path>` for every contributing implementation
and repair record of the candidate, including continuations. Use the bound code
checkout, never cwd or the split-root state checkout. `repair` resolves the
implementation row. The command reads a clean committed snapshot, validates all
three rows and emits JSON; it writes no settings, state or dispatches.

Exit 0 with `source=readme-default` means absent: retain today's README model and
host behavior without a question or fabricated effort. Exit 1 names invalid,
uncommitted, unreadable or unsupported present data: return it to FO; no fallback.
A committed deletion restores README behavior. Recommendations never update an
accepted snapshot. For configured settings use Paseo's existing Codex route; a
native route request returns to FO.

Keep `Model:` and add this header to the normal dispatch record, using resolver
values rather than copying the recommendation:

```text
Roster: source=repository; role=implementation; provider=codex; model=gpt-6.1-sol; effort=high; host=paseo; digest=sha256:DIGEST; commit=SHA
```

For absence use `Roster: absent; source README default`. For validation retain all
author references/tuples and `family` in the record and existing report/gate summary.
Sol and Astra share OpenAI provider lineage: `same-family: openai` is informational,
not a refusal or diversity claim. Missing/unknown author evidence is `unverified`.
The resolver understands these Roster headers and historical `Model: MODEL (Codex
via Paseo, thinking EFFORT;...)` headers; other formats remain unverified. Existing
names/folder/coverage/law checks remain due but do not prove roster consumption.

Preflight live provider/model/effort capability, listed extension eligibility,
workspace placement, permissions and existing worker identity before build.
Preserve generated prompt, identity and runtime fields. A non-null generated
model/effort conflicting with the tuple is a transport mismatch: return to FO,
never patch the envelope. Pass provider/model and `settings.thinkingOptionId`
beside those fields on the existing Paseo route. After successful build immediately
spawn, then save its handle; checks and narration precede build.

A continuation resolves again and records its source. Reuse only when its effective
tuple matches the existing worker; changed tuples return to FO for authorized
fresh handoff, without mutating or duplicating a running worker. Capacity, network
and uncertain launches use current manual recovery, without model substitution.
Keep requested settings separate from supported child runtime/turn evidence of
actual model, effort, root and preserved permissions; echo or worker assertion
alone is insufficient. Missing decisive evidence returns to FO.

FO and special roles retain current model floors, triggers and delivery duties,
including the Paseo worker-local commit and FO publication/review split. This
slice adds no personal store, capacity automation, new law, special-role hosting,
native adapter or additional provider.
